Bluetooth does cater for high quality audio codecs. The problem is that every device is slightly different and if even one device in the path doesn't support a specific BT profile, the path drops to the lowest common denominator.

Say your headphone (the BT sink) caters for 24bit uncompressed audio. (TBH, it's been a while since I read the specifications, so I don't know if the profile exists.)

Your source should cater for the same profile. What I've observed in real life is quite random. If it's a pure headphone, it should connect with high quality audio. If it's a headset (i.e. it has a mic), it might connect as a headset with reduced audio quality. The order in which you power up the devices changes things. The last device to connect to the headphone/headset can leave behind preferred settings, so the headphone needs to be unpaired and re-paired every time. This is an extreme example, which most anyone can hear, but I'm very skeptical of people who claim they can hear the difference between 24 bit uncompressed audio and 16 bit uncompressed audio. And at my age, where hearing loss above 12khz is practically guaranteed, it's another story.

In short, while every device might cater for high quality audio, the actual connection depends on runtime conditions, which I for one, haven't found a solution which nails it down to 100% reliability.
